content: The following findings are based on time series analyses from various studies: 1. O'Farrell (2006) conducted a study in Lao PDR, which demonstrated that both NG (Neisseria gonorrhoeae) and CT (Chlamydia trachomatis) rates were lower. 2. Wi (2006) analyzed data from the Philippines, showing that NG and CT rates were lower, while CU (condom use) rates were higher. 3. McKormick (2007) studied trends in Bangladesh, finding that NG and CT rates were lower, CU rates were also lower, and PSA (prostate-specific antigen) levels were reduced. 4. Bollen (2010) examined data from Indonesia, reporting lower NG and CT rates, but higher CU rates. 5. Bruce (2011) investigated trends in Papua New Guinea, identifying lower NG and CT rates alongside higher CU rates.
